name: Logseq
tagline: A local-first outliner and personal knowledge graph
description: A note-taking app built around bullet-point outlines, daily journals, backlinks and queries. Everything is stored on your own device. It is a personal knowledge tool first; team features are only beginning to arrive.
licenseNote: The apps are free and open source. Hosted sync is an optional paid extra.

maturity.rationale: Loved by its users, but in transition: in 2026 the project split into the original Markdown-file app (now 'Logseq OG', maintenance only) and a database-backed Logseq 2.0 that is still in beta. Choose knowingly.

strengths: Your notes stay with you: plain Markdown files in Logseq OG, a local database in 2.0
Backlinks, block references and queries make a personal knowledge base genuinely useful
Works offline by design; the file-based version syncs with any file tool such as Syncthing or Git
weaknesses: A personal tool, not a team wiki: no workspace permissions, and real-time collaboration is still alpha in the database version
The file-based app and the newer database-backed one are separate, and the newer one is less mature
Mobile apps and sync have historically been the rough edges

featureNotes.realtime-collab: Alpha, in the database version only
featureNotes.databases: Properties, queries and tables; richer in the database version
featureNotes.plain-files: In Logseq OG; version 2.0 uses a local database with Markdown export
featureNotes.public-sharing: Publishes a graph as a static site
featureNotes.notion-import: Via Notion's Markdown export, with manual clean-up
